That is, you can expect that evidence will be elicited from this witness in this and this area. Now, if you say 92 ter, that's what we are most likely not deal with extensively in court and, apart from that, especially other areas could be covered, so then it must be clear to the Defence what those other areas could be apart from the 92 ter material. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, and I think it's clear from our filings and submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, and then your next step is that you say, well, from the previous testimony and from the proofing note which was disclosed at the time at the first start of this trial, that's where the Defence was put on notice that this is what they could expect. That's your reasoning. Whereas, if I understand the Defence well -- first of all, the status of any activity undertaken at that time, we might have to consider that as well because evidence is not evidence heard by this Chamber. At the same time, the exchange of information between the parties is not necessarily excluded. It's not that we repeat the whole of the -- the out-of-court and the pre-trial matters that were the subject of exchange between the parties. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: For Your Honours's information, the Prosecution's Rule 65 ter summary does not include this evidence. At paragraph 6, it simply says: "Finally the witness will testify about the presence of paramilitary units in Eastern Slavonia in the late summer/fall of 1991, including units led by Arkan. Whilst operating in Eastern Slavonia, Arkan was subject to Radovan -- subordinate to Radovan Stojicic, an official of the MUP of Serbia." That's the sum total of the discussion in the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you specifically draw the attention in the 65 ter summary by the paramilitary's led by Arkan, would you then expect that on the basis of the general observation, that the Defence could understand that you would elicit evidence also on any groups that were led by one of the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Well, the point being, you see, I think the chronology. We obviously understand 65 ter to guarantee that the Defence is put on notice. Now, the proofing note at issue has been submitted after that 65 ter summary, as well as the testimony that had happened in 2008 has happened afterwards. It may well be that we should have filed an amended 65 ter summary, but with all that notice, I'm still having trouble to see the prejudice of the Defence, especially if they have expected me to cover that area as was earlier said today.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm sorry to keep leaping up and down, Your Honours, the comment about expecting the Prosecution to do that is premised on the fact that the Prosecution clearly intended to elicit the evidence. And so we would have expected the Prosecution to speak to the witness about it in the proofing sessions because they clearly intended to lead it. What we are complaining about is that we were never told about that intention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, during proofing sessions with this witness, has this matter been dealt with?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, and that's why we compiled that proofing note which was disclosed two years ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but in the most recent proofing sessions. I mean, we received a new proofing note.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, of course, but the latest proofing note doesn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what you say --

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: -- repeat what was earlier notified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you say is that it didn't have to be contained in your proofing note because it was already in the proofing note two years ago which was then followed by evidence on the matter in this case, which case then restarted after that. Anything to add at this moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will take some time to consider how to proceed and everyone is expected to remain standby. --- Break taken at 5.02 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber allows the Prosecution to deal with the subject matter to which objections were raised. At the same time, the Chamber also is aware that it is a bit of a confusing situation, and there may be a difference between the Stanisic Defence and the Simatovic Defence. The fact that evidence that was heard earlier, that this Chamber cannot rely on this evidence, of course we cannot because there are other judges and that's not -- we have restarted that case which does not automatically mean that nothing that has happened before or that everything that happened before lost all of its relevance or importance. At the same time, Mr. Hoffmann, it would have been preferable to make these matters clear. I mean, the confusion exists partly due to the fact that you were not explicit in these matters. To some extent, although this may be less valid for the Stanisic Defence as it is for the Simatovic Defence, to some extent the Chamber understands that if they have to dig up all pieces of information that were there earlier, that that makes it difficult, although, as I said before, less difficult for the Stanisic Defence because they were present when this evidence was elicited. They were -- they received the proofing note at the time which, by the way, as I understand, was not received by the Chamber. So, therefore, it needed less imagination that the same matter would be covered by the present testimony. Of course, for the Simatovic Defence, it's to some extent different. The Chamber is, of course, not aware to what extent disclosed proofing notes finally were received by the Simatovic Defence. At least these counsel were not present during the earlier testimony when the case was started. If I were Defence counsel, I would have read that transcript of only one witness. So it's -- I think both sides are to be blamed to a certain extent for the confusion that exists at this moment. Under those circumstances, we allow you to continue, but the Chamber will entertain any request for further remedies if the Defence considers that it needs to further prepare for cross-examination. Again, we are not going to postpone all of the cross-examination, but if there's any specific request and if good cause is shown for that, we'll certainly consider any additional remedy sought by the -- or any remedy sought by the Defence. The other matter on which we'll hear further submissions today, that is, amending the 65 ter summary, is of a similar nature, and when discussing what to do with that this morning, an observation was made, during a meeting, which was about kids that start learning to -- how to use a bike. During the first few days, you would expect the kids to come back home with blood on their knees and bandages to be ready. After a certain moment, the mothers will put back the bandages in the cupboard and would expect that only exceptionally the kids would come back to them with bloodied knees. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, let me take the groups that you mentioned quickly one by one. You mentioned Frenki's Men. Can you please explain to the Court who Frenki was, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Frenki Simatovic was one of the top people in the MUP of Serbia. I really don't know what his exact position was at the time. Whether he was in charge of the Special Police Unit or of a detachment within the MUP of Serbia, I really wouldn't know for that particular period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. And you referred to another group called Badza's Men. Can you tell who was Badza?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Radovan Stojicic, Badza, was at the time either the deputy or -- no, I think he was the commander of the Special Brigade. The Special Police Unit in the Republican SUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Do you have any knowledge if any of those units that you mentioned a few minutes ago had any relationship among themselves?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I object again. With your leave, the witness said that as for -- that he heard from old people who could not distinguish who was who, that they said that there were people coming there, groups. And now the Prosecutor is asking him to talk about their mutual relations and on the basis of what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, this observation is appropriately to be made when the witness doesn't follow the proceedings. Could you take off your earphones for a second. Mr. Petrovic, I do understand that you are asking for foundation, factual knowledge which would create the foundation for the questions put by Mr. Hoffmann; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, you are invited to lay your foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: My intention was to do so, but first elicit if he has any information, then to see what the source of that information is, with Your Honours' leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the answer to the previous questions would justify the opposite order of proceeding. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned that you had talked to people in the villages about the presence of those paramilitary units that you mentioned. Did you have any other source of information with regard to those paramilitary units while you were in Osijek or Beli Manastir? And if you could just, if any, list any such source.

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Can we deal with this in closed session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, if you look at the letterhead, the stamp, and the people -- the person who signed this document, this report from the federal state security service, would you say that this document is authentic?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: This report relates to pressure on Croats and Slovaks in the SAO SBWS and to the presence of various paramilitary units. And that reference is to be found on page 3, last paragraph in English, and page 4, paragraph 2 in B/C/S. And having reviewed that document prior to court, would you say that this report is in substance consistent with your knowledge of the situation in the area?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Well, as far as I could see, this document clearly shows that Ilok was part of that territory and that it can be -- that it is consistent with the situation as it was in the field. At least the areas where I was, in Beli Manastir and the area towards Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Was it a normal procedure that the federal DB would report to the Serbian DB here on a situation that actually occurred on the territory of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: There were such instances because the border area towards Serbia was Serbia. It belonged to Serbia. We, from the federal ministry, were not competent as far as the war-time situation was and the activities, and we did not get involved in the general crime because the federal administration and the state security service, and I'm talking about my service, for us, these were matters of no interest because all these individuals acted publicly and their activities were public. So they weren't of any interest as far as intelligence was concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, I would tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be? HE REGISTRAR: This would be Exhibit P428, Your Honours. I apologise, P429, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P429 is admitted into evidence. I'd like to, before we --

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Could I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: -- ask that it be at least provisionally put under seal until the issue of possible redactions is sorted out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is admitted under seal. I want to put on the record the following: That where the transcript says that P427, that is a video which was announced as being 65 ter 4718, that that was admitted into evidence, that we should be aware that it was uploaded in e-court as 65 ter 4718.2. Then one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, you've used approximately your two hours. Would that mean that you would need now time after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I would appreciate if I could have maybe another 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ten minutes. Please organise yourself in such a way that ten minutes will be enough. We'll have a break and we'll resume at five minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, your ten minutes have started.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecution will play just one more little clip, again from Exhibit P18, the interview with Vojislav Seselj. For the booth this is clip 5. It starts at minute 46.14 in the original tape.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Reporter: What was the objective of your battle over there? Was it to separate the Croats and the Serbs so they wouldn't live in the same state anymore? What was really the objective? "Seselj: The objective of our fight was to keep Serbian territories. We never wanted any Croatian territories. Our soldiers never endangered any undeniably Croatian territories. But we didn't want to let the Croats take the Serbian territories out of Yugoslavia. That was the basic objective, and we achieved about 70 per cent of that objective."

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Witness, very briefly, having heard what Seselj said here in 1995, is that consistent with the speeches that you heard of Seselj earlier onwards?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Well, do you mean at that time or is it a reference to an earlier period? Do you mean 1995 or earlier on, whether he said the same things earlier on?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: The latter, if he had said similar things in previous years?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Well, yes, he said in the statement himself that he understood, after he returned from America, that he saw what he saw and he confirmed it, and he also always spoke about Greater Serbia and the interests of Greater Serbia and the Serbian people in all of his speeches.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hoffmann. Who will be the first to cross-examine the witness, will it be the Stanisic Defence or --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The Stanisic Defence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness JF-038, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Jordash. Mr. Jordash is counsel for Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me just start with a couple of preliminaries.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: With reference to the two clips from the Seselj video we've seen, you commented earlier, and I para-phrase, that depending on the area in which he gave the speech, it would differ a little but the objective was the same. What was the objective which was the same, according to you?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Well, in almost all of his speeches he spoke about the establishment of Greater Serbia by linking up certain territories from the former Yugoslavia that belonged to Croatia, Bosnia, and linking them up with Serbia and thus establishing the Greater Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. So he would tailor his speech to the audience in order to express his consistent objective; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Have you listened to several of his speeches over the years?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Well, I did not listen them in their entirety. First of all, I wasn't really attracted to them, nor was I particularly interested in that aspect, but in just reading up a little bit on it, you could figure out what he was saying. For instance, if he was speaking in Kragujevac, Uzice or Kraljevo, in other words in central Serbia, there would be a speech, at least as far as I could see, the impressions that I got as compared to, for instance, when he was in Vojvodina where he also had speeches. And I believe that once when he was in Kosovo, he was even detained by the police. Where his speech had a direct impact on the people who lived there in the territory, the speech would be far sharper and far more extreme than the speech he would give in Kraljevo, for instance, because there, he wouldn't have to point out his Serbianhood, as it were -- Serbhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, he would say what he wanted basically to achieve his aims. Is that the impression you got from the speeches you in part listened to?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Well, yes, and after all the events and developments and based on information we had from the service itself, his objective was one in the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I have -- let's move to a different subject. Could I have, please, on the e-court, Exhibit P429. Did I record the [Microphone not activated] ... Sorry, it's 65 ter 4826 but it has been given an exhibit number which I -- it is P429, I'm told, which is I hope what I said. Yes, P429. Your Honours, page 59 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Just for the same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Just for the same reasons given before, I would ask that it not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Registry instructed not to broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I just wanted you to have a look at that and just remind you of something you said so I can ask you further about it. Your Honours, page 59 of the transcript today, you were asked by Mr. Hoffmann, for the Prosecution, whether it was normal procedure that the federal DB would report to the Serbian DB on a situation that occurred on the territory of the Republic of Croatia. And you answered: "There were such instances because the border area towards Serbia was Serbia. It belonged to Serbia." Were you suggesting there that this was not normal procedure to report to the Serbian DB, but when it directly concerned the border, there might be reports?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: This is not a report from the service. These are notes and you should make a distinction between the two. These are notes by a member of the federal ministry. As for a report, we have certain rules as to how they are drafted, and I'm referring to our -- in our rules, but there were instances where we would inform various republics, including Serbia, about intelligence that we obtained because as a federal service and a federal Ministry of the Interior, we could not really take action on a territory without the knowledge of the competent authorities on that territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you for the explanation. The point I'm trying to understand is your answer to the Prosecution when you said there were such instances of, let's put it neutrally, relaying information from the federal DB to the Serbian DB, and you appeared to suggest it occurred when the issue related to the border area towards Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So that was when the federal DB would relay information, when it concerned the territorial integrity of Serbia; is that correct? In the time-frame we are looking at in this report, April of 1992. Can you answer so the transcript can be --

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And when it concerned matters within this report, matters which you termed "general crime," there wasn't a consistent or normal practice of reporting to the Serbian DB; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Well, I cannot really say with certainty because I was not an employee of that service. But in any case, no matter what type of information that was being conveyed, whether it was an Official Note or just sending them data and information that our service obtained, but certainly the federal service also had a certain instructor role, but we did not really deal with the problems in the field on the ground in various republics, and to be more specific, without the presence of the members of the Republic of Serbia, or rather, the ministry of the Republic of Serbia. I don't know how else to describe this. Because we did not have the personnel or any operative conditions where we could actually take action in the field, so our role was really to -- to give guidance and instructions and to compare and sort of review as to how far we have accomplished certain goals or resolve certain problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can we turn, please, to page 3 of this report. And I'm interested in the last paragraph, which should start: "In the last seven days alone ..." Could we go to page 3 in the English and B/C/S, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could you just read that to yourself, Mr. Witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can we go to the bottom of the page in the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this the third page, what I have before me? Because it is not consistent with the English version. I'm reading what is written in Serbian and it doesn't correspond to what I see in the English version because some names are mentioned there. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can we go to page 4 of the B/C/S and see if we can find that paragraph. I'm looking for the paragraph: "In the last seven days alone, Stevo Tinkotski from Bapska ..." Can we see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's now -- it's the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Second paragraph, thank you. Sorry for the delay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can you just read that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Well, something isn't really consistent here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Just read the whole paragraph and then tell us what is, in your view, not consistent.

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: I don't see the page number, but all I can say is that it still doesn't correspond to the English version. Just the last portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The pages are not the same. Would you please focus exclusively on the second paragraph, the middle paragraph you see on your screen, that's what Mr. Jordash wants you to read.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have read it. So what is the issue? What am I supposed to comment on?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The information I'm focusing on is the information that appears to have been sent to the Serbian DB in April of 1992 concerning Bozovic being a member of the Serbian guard. Was that something that you were told at the time? Is that something you became aware of around that time?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Bozovic, or Beli as he was called, was not a member of the Serb guard, but rather of the White Eagles. He was with Vuk Draskovic. He had dealings with Vuk Draskovic. If that's the Bozovic that is mentioned here. Yes, it says multicoloured uniforms of the Serbian guard. I don't know whether this refers to Giska or to Beli, but I do remember the name, and he belonged to the SPO or the White Eagles.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know agree with this categorisation that is in the paragraph, no one knows who is who and who commands whom anymore. Was that the problem with the information you were receiving in April of 1992? You'll have to speak rather than nod, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Yes, that was the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's turn now to page 4 in the English version and

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you have that paragraph, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It appears that representatives of the federal SUP were reporting to the Serbian DB that in relation to the crimes in Ilok, they undertook to inform the government and the Ministry of the Interior of the Serbian Republic of Krajina to take necessary measures. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Why was it that the federal SUP --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Perhaps we should go into closed session so the witness can answer the question, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private into session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Again, I don't want to discuss what the law was and your expectation that the Croatian authorities would have jurisdiction by law. What I'm talking about is de facto, the reality on the ground at the time. Did you and others, your colleagues, regard the Ministry of the Interior of the Serbian Republic of Krajina as the competent authority? Yes or no I think might suffice for this one.

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: No. No. If you are talking about --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Who did you regard as the competent authority for dealing with crimes in Ilok then?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: It was the territory of Croatia and the Croatian ministry. Again, I'm saying it's easy to discuss things now, from here, but it was different, the situation was different in those times of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If that's your answer, we can move on. Thank you. Now, Gracanin, according to you, was appointed as federal minister by Milosevic; is that a fair summary of your position today?

utterances.speaker: JF-038
utterances.text: Briefly, clearly, as far as I'm concerned, no. But in a certain situation, the one that prevailed then, it was somebody from Slovenia or Macedonia that was supposed to send someone to become minster. However, they had cut off all relation with the federation and federal organs, and then they probably wanted to have more personnel there. And bearing in mind the fact that before holding this office, Petar Gracanin had been president of the Presidency of Serbia, he could not have come to hold this office without Milosevic's knowing about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think Madam has had a crash.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I missed that. I am afraid that we get all of the beginning of today's transcript again, and then Judge Hall appears and others who have not been present in this courtroom today, and that's where the computers take over rather than ... I am afraid that we have to accept that the transcript broke down and that all the attempts to restore it -- on my right screen I get a totally different picture compared to my left screen, that it has to be restored. Now, I had on my mind that we would spend the last ten minutes on hearing the submissions in relation to the motion which was filed by the Prosecution. Now, I am aware that what I say now is maybe translated and maybe recorded audio/video, and I'm looking at the transcriber, apparently she's trying to get this language in the computer, although it's not visible on our screens, that it arrives there. What I hope that will happen is that once the text stops moving on our screens, that we are at a point where we at least have a transcript again, and that would be approximately at page 60 or 65, I take it, whereas we are now at close to 38. I am afraid that we have to give up for today because I wouldn't -- unless -- unless the parties would be willing to make their submissions without the transcript and to have it put on the record in one way or another because it is an urgent matter, because the witness may already arrive tomorrow. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I can make a suggestion, maybe exceptionally this time both Defence counsel could make their submissions in an e-mail which then could be read into the record at some point in the future when it is working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jordash explained to us that he asked to make oral submissions because he didn't have time to --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'd prepared -- I can put my submissions very simply. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but only with the consent of all parties, this Chamber would be willing to hear the submission and then we would have to find a way to put it on the record at a later stage because it would then be as if we are hearing something out of court which then is put on the record at a later stage. If all parties agree with such procedure, then I have to consult with my colleagues whether that would be acceptable for them as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My colleagues agree, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Well, I understand from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we can -- yes. Before we hear your submission, Mr. Jordash, we better already excuse the witness. We have a technical problem, but we would have concluded anyhow at this time, so therefore, Witness JF-038, I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak to anyone or communicate in any other way with anyone about the testimony you've given or the testimony which is still to be given starting tomorrow. We'd like to see you back tomorrow, quarter past 2.00, in this same courtroom. The Usher will now escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. As I indicated, I'll put my submissions very simply. I understand from the chronology that Your Honours gave earlier that Your Honours are likely to be against the submissions, so I will be very brief, but it is a question, as Your Honours will appreciate, of notice. At one point the indictment against these two accused included something of the events in Vukovar. It no longer does include those events. We were told in the Rule 65 ter summary that this witness would testify about effectively force -- forcible transfer of civilians and unlawful killing of civilians in Skelani and villages along the Serbian border within Bosnia. The Prosecution, with their application, seek to introduce a whole range of completely different issues into the trial; namely, those issues which relate to the events in Vukovar, a return to their original case against the accused. I premised -- sorry. I qualify this submission with one caveat which is that the Prosecution have not indicated what they allege is the probative value of this evidence, but as it stands, the Defence have to mount a rebuttal of allegations which effectively put Mr. Simatovic at the centre of events in Vukovar. The latest proofing note from this witness speaks of Frenki's Men and Arkan's Men going into the town of Vukovar to fight and then withdraw to the surrounding positions. So this evidence, what it does is it puts the Defence into the position of having to, one, investigate a whole new crime base; two, cross-examine on the fruits of that investigation and seek to undermine the inference the Prosecution want to make. We now have to investigate Vukovar. We now have to cross-examine on those events. This is not a situation where the Prosecution is simply saying well, what we're interested in is the training in Mount Tara, which was a precursor to troops then going into Vukovar. We are not interested in the events in Vukovar. This is a situation where, as time has gone on, the Prosecution have sought to adduce fresh evidence about direct participation in crimes by Mr. Simatovic and, by inference, Mr. Stanisic. Those are our objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Groome, very brief response to start with.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just briefly. It seems to me that the 65 ter deals with two things: One is notice to the accused so they can prepare their case; it also provides the Chamber with the essence of what the witness will testify to so that the witness -- so that the Chamber can manage the case, can make decisions about whether to require the Prosecution to reduce its case. It seems we are talking about here about notice. As the Chamber has pointed out earlier today, the Prosecution has been very consistent in its statement or its assertion that it would be seeking to introduce all of the testimony. We have never, ever, waivered from that. It is when I discovered a technical breach of the 65 ter that we -- that the person who wrote it did not properly summarise all of the material we gave notice we were going to introduce, that I asked that a submission be prepared to correct that. I'd also point out, although the Prosecution has dropped the killings in Vukovar, the Prosecution charges or the indictment charges persecution and deportation/forcible transfer of the entire SAO SBWS, which includes the Vukovar area. So there can be no mistake that although the killings have been dropped, the events of Vukovar are still relevant to this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, you are the responding party, any need to make further submissions, which should be limited in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can I just have a moment just to read what Mr. Groome has said, just ten seconds will do it. I think Your Honours have our submission. A technical breach of the Rule 65 ter may be a technical breach for the Prosecution. For us, we use the Rule 65 ter documents as an indication of what a witness is going to say and an indication of what investigation we must conduct. We have not conducted any investigation into the Vukovar incident because it isn't in the Rule 65 ter notice document. And whilst the Prosecution are technical correct insofar as they say the indictment includes the whole of the SBWS, it's a very different situation to have specific allegations of direct participation which require specific investigation. Forcible transfer of the entire SBWS requires investigation into what evidence -- sorry, what we've been told is going to be led through the vehicle of the Rule 65 ter document. It doesn't require us to go to the whole of the SBWS and investigate every single town and village. Those are our submissions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn for the day. We have a transcript again on our screen which means that the adjournment and especially when we'll resume is clearly put on the record. We adjourn and we resume tomorrow, the 13th of May, quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon, in this same courtroom, II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 13th day of May, 2010, at 2.15 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
